title: N-bearing complex organics toward high-mass protostars. Constant ratios pointing to formation in similar pre-stellar conditions across a large mass range
question: Study six N-bearing complex organic molecules (CH3CN, HNCO, NH2CHO, C2H5CN, C2H3CN, CH3NH2) and CH3OH in 37 line-rich high-mass protostars to determine excitation temperatures, column density ratios, and formation conditions across low- and high-mass protostars.

recipe.goal: Select sample of 37 line-rich hot molecular cores and extract single-pixel spectra
recipe.method: Select sources from ~200 publicly available ALMAGAL pipeline products (beam 0.5''-1.5'') where CH3CN 12_7-11_7 is detected at ~2.5-3 sigma, excluding sources with very blended lines; extract spectrum from the peak pixel of the CH3CN 12_4-11_4 moment zero map (1 beam off-source for 787212).
assumptions: CH3CN 12_4-11_4 traces the overall N-bearing COM emission

recipe.goal: Fit LTE synthetic spectra to derive column densities, excitation temperatures, and FWHMs
recipe.method: Use CASSIS assuming LTE with a single velocity component. Apply chi^2 grid fitting for species with relatively unblended lines (C2H3CN, C2H5CN, some CH3^18OH) and fit-by-eye for blended species (HN^13CO, CH3^13CN, NH2CHO, CH3NH2, ^13CH3OH, most CH3^18OH). Fit blending contaminants (C2H3CN, NH2CN, C2H5OH) prior to fitting NH2CHO.
key_parameters: Grid N: 10^13 to 10^17 cm^-2 in steps of 0.1 dex; Grid T_ex: 10 to 300 K in steps of 10 K; Grid FWHM: 3 to 11 km s^-1 in steps of 0.1 km s^-1
Fixed T_ex when not fitted: fixed to T_ex of CH3^13CN (~150 K if CH3^13CN not fitted), or 90 K for CH3NH2 (60 K for G345.5043+00.3480)
Vibrational correction factors: 1.5 at 300 K for NH2CHO; 1.3174 to 2.1318 for C2H5CN at T_ex >= 120 K; ignored (<1.1) for CH3CN
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), single velocity component, and beam dilution factor of unity

recipe.goal: Convert isotopologue column densities to main isotopologues (CH3CN, HNCO, CH3OH)
recipe.method: Multiply column densities of CH3^13CN, HN^13CO, and CH3^18OH (or ^13CH3OH) by Galactocentric-distance-dependent 12C/13C and 16O/18O ratios; when isotopologues are undetected, blended, or optically thicker than weak main lines, fit the weakest clearly detected (S/N > 3) main line (e.g., CH3CN 12_10-11_10).
key_parameters: Sun's Galactocentric distance = 8.05 kpc; typical distance uncertainty = 0.5 kpc; 12C/13C = 34 to 70 (error 6-12); 16O/18O = 188 to 525 (error 75-116)
assumptions: Isotopologue ratios follow the linear Galactocentric gradient relations of Wilson & Rood (1994) and Milam et al. (2005); y-intercept uncertainty is omitted from error propagation

recipe.goal: Compute column density correlations, power-law fits, and spread factors across low- and high-mass protostars
recipe.method: Calculate Pearson's r correlation coefficients in log10 space between column densities (excluding ^13CH3OH-derived methanol sources); fit power-law between NH2CHO and HNCO; compute error-weighted mean and 1-sigma spread factor (10^dex) of log10 column density ratios combining ALMAGAL and literature low/high-mass sources (excluding upper/lower limits and Sgr B2(N2)).
key_parameters: N_H2 = 10^23 cm^-2 assumed to normalize literature abundance fits in NH2CHO vs HNCO comparison
assumptions: Emitting areas of the two species in a ratio are assumed equal (prior to physical structure corrections)

recipe.goal: Model pre-stellar timescale scatter using a chemical toy model and compare ratios with Garrod et al. (2022) models
recipe.method: Compare observed column density ratios with peak gas-phase abundances from Garrod et al. (2022) warm-up models; parameterize pre-stellar ice abundance growth between 10^5 and 10^6 yr as X_i = A_i (t / 10^6 yr)^alpha_i to infer the spread in pre-stellar timescales (t / t_bar) from the observed spread in abundance ratios.
key_parameters: alpha values: CH3CN = 3.7, C2H5CN = 3.0, CH3OH = 2.3, HNCO = 3.9, C2H3CN = 4.0, CH3NH2 = 1.3; pre-stellar timescale range 10^5 to 10^6 yr
assumptions: Column density ratios equal pre-stellar ice abundance ratios; pre-stellar temperature is constant at ~10 K and density increases from ~10^3 to ~10^8 cm^-3

score_reason: The paper uses standard public archival pipeline products (2019.1.00195.L) as-is, and provides exact extraction coordinates, beam sizes, RMS values, source velocities, isotope ratios, vibrational correction factors, line lists (for N-bearing species), and complete per-source fit tables. Reproducibility is slightly limited by the reliance on manual 'fit-by-eye' spectral modeling in CASSIS for blended species and the omission of the methanol line list from Table 4.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA pipeline data products are public in the archive, the exact sky coordinates for single-pixel spectrum extraction are tabulated for all 37 sources, and the main results (per-source LTE column densities, excitation temperatures, Pearson correlations, and ratio spread factors) are fully numeric.
